reason: E2 directly supports that an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with a composite lamellar architecture improves strength–ductility synergy in AlCoCrFeNi2.1, but it does not mention cold rolling or annealing as the processing route. E1 describes the as-cast properties as an 'unprecedented combination' of strength and ductility, contradicting the premise that the starting state is suboptimal. No cited evidence supports the claims about improved creep or corrosion resistance.
premises: Cold rolling (~8%) and low-temperature annealing can refine the lamellar structure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA into an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure.
An ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with a composite lamellar architecture improves strength–ductility synergy in this alloy.
The proposed treatment will enhance room-temperature creep resistance.
The proposed treatment will improve corrosion resistance.
The as-cast fine lamellar state has suboptimal mechanical performance below industrial requirements.
